Pool fractions

Source: R/terms.R
frac_pool.Rd

The sum of the numerators over the sum of the denominators, which pools proportions such as 3 of 10 and 30 of 100 into 33 of 110.

Usage

frac_pool(x, na.rm = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A fraction() vector.

na.rm

Should missing values be removed?

Value

A fraction() of size 1, which isn't reduced to lowest terms. It is 0/0 if x is empty, and missing if any elements of x are missing.

Details

Unlike mean(), which weights all fractions equally, frac_pool() weights fractions by their denominators. So it depends on how fractions are written: pooling 1/2 with 0/1 is 1/3, but pooling 2/4 with 0/1 is 2/5. Calculations reduce fractions to lowest terms, so pool the original fractions.

0/0 contributes nothing to the total, and 1/0 or -1/0 give the same result (or 0/0 if there are both). Totals larger than 2^53 are missing, with a warning.

Examples

x <- fraction(c(3, 30, 1), c(10, 100, 2))
frac_pool(x)
#> <fraction<double>[1]>
#> [1] 34/112
mean(x)
#> <fraction<double>[1]>
#> [1] 11/30
